title: Filigree Pay — opportunity jotter
content:
Quick personal scratch notes for Filigree Pay outreach — super rough. Meant to capture account signals, outreach drafts, objection handling, and a 2-week pilot sketch. Not for SOC review yet.

ACCOUNT SNAPSHOT (raw):
- Company: Filigree Pay (mid-market fintech, BNPL + merchant payouts)
- HQ: Denver, CO; engineering ~120, platform/infra ~20; recently raised a Series B (rumored +$60M)
- Public signals: hiring for inference/embedding roles, blog post about "real-time personalization at scale", uses GCP and private data stores, early mention of "latency-sensitive fraud scoring" in job descriptions.
- Tech stack guesses: Python services, k8s, GKE, Redis, BigQuery; experimenting with LLM-based customer support + internal search.
- Why this matters: likely cares about predictable per-token cost for production LLMs + low tail latency for fraud/UX use-cases.

KEY PEOPLE (to confirm):
- CTPO / Head of Engineering: Maya D'Silva (look for posts) — likely exec budget holder.
- Head of ML / ML Eng: Ravi Patel — buyer/operator for model hosting decisions.
- Platform Eng lead: Jonah Park — cares about ops, rollout, SLA.
- Product lead (payments): Liana Ortiz — cares about accuracy/regulatory controls.

PAIN / TL;DR HYPOTHESIS:
- They need: deterministic latency for inference (fraud scoring), cost predictability for embeddings/search across many tenants, private deployment options for sensitive payouts data, and easy rollback/rollouts for models used in compliance.
- Current friction: relying on a mix of hosted endpoints + DIY GPU infra leads to inconsistent p99 latency and surprise token bills during spikes (marketing/seasonal).

EVIDENCE / SIGNALS:
- Job postings that mention "real-time inference" and "<100ms decisions".
- Open-source SDKs in their repos referencing OpenAI + on-prem experiments.
- Blog describing a ML feature release slowed by infra flakiness.

OUTREACH STRATEGY (two-parallel flows):
A) Technical-first: target Ravi (Head of ML) + Jonah (platform). Pitch a 2-week pilot on Redwood Private or Dedicated focusing on their fraud scoring pipeline. Emphasize latency SLOs, canary rollouts, KV/prefix caching to cut per-token compute, and cost forecasts. Ask for a raw sample inference trace and sequence lengths.
B) Product/Business: target Liana + Maya. Pitch predictable billing + compliance controls. Frame Redwood as way to reduce MTTR for model regressions and keep product velocity with rollback policies.

COLD EMAIL DRAFTS (keep short) — pick tone based on persona:
1) Technical (Ravi) — subject: "2-week pilot to stabilize fraud LLM latency at Filigree"
Hi Ravi — quick note: we helped a payments team move their fraud scoring to a dedicated inference runtime and reduced p99 from ~400ms to ~80ms while cutting token spend 30% via KV caching and batching. Wondering if a short pilot to run a copy of your scoring model (or a compatible variant) on dedicated capacity makes sense — can show latency/cost before you commit. If interested, I can sync with your platform lead for a 20m tech call.
2) Product (Liana) — subject: "Avoid surprise LLM bills during peak payouts"
Hi Liana — noticed Filigree runs several ML features that touch payouts. We help teams lock down predictable per-feature inference costs and provide controlled rollouts and audit logs for regulated flows. Short pilot plan attached. Would love 10–15m to see if this maps to your priorities.

CALL / VOICEMAIL SCRIPT (30s):
- Quick intro (name + Redwood). One-line value: "we give engineering teams predictable latency and costs for LLMs across hosted and private installs".
- Ask: "who owns model serving decisions for fraud/product search?"
- Close with an offer: "20 minute technical review with our solutions engineer + a pilot proposal in the same week."

OBJECTIONS & REBUTTALS (live notes):
- "We already have infra": Great; ask how they measure p99 and cost per inference. Offer an apples-to-apples pilot: run same model/trace and show delta in cost/latency.
- "Security/compliance concerns": Highlight Redwood Private + VPC option, KMS integration, audit logs. Offer NDAs and a 1-node air-gapped evaluation if they request.
- "No budget": Offer a time-boxed evaluation funded by Redwood (intro trial credits) — positioned as risk-free to validate numbers.
- "Lock-in concerns": Emphasize open model support, standard formats (HF checkpoints), canary rollbacks, and no runtime-level vendor lock-in for model artifacts.
- "We use X provider (OpenAI) for quality": Propose hybrid routing — keep quality-critical reads on hosted models while using Redwood Dedicated as fallthrough for cost-critical paths.

DISCOVERY QUESTIONS (for first call):
- What is your current p50/p95/p99 for the fraud scoring path?
- Token sequence length distribution for that path (median + 95th)?
- What model family/architecture are you using (Llama2, Falcon, in-house)?
- Throughput (req/s) during peak and typical? Spiky patterns?
- Are there compliance/regulatory constraints around model outputs or data residency?
- Who needs access to logs/traceability for audits?

PILOT SKETCH (2-week):
- Day 0–2: onboarding + access + sample traces + small infra provisioning (dev/staging instance on Redwood Dedicated or Private).
- Day 3–7: run production-like traffic replay (we replay traces you provide) and measure latency / cost, tune batching/quantization profile, test prefix caching on repeated sequences.
- Day 8–10: canary integration with a shadow/real traffic route, observe fallback behavior and rollback flows.
- Day 11–14: finalize report with p99 improvement, cost delta, and recommended config for rollout.
Success metrics: reduce p99 by X ms (goal: >2x improvement vs current), reduce token compute cost by >20%, no production errors during canary.

INTERNAL ASK (for solutions eng + product folks):
- Need a SE (Diego) assigned for direct tech call.
- Request a short SOW template + trial credits approval.
- Possible quantization/config recipe for common sequence lengths (ask applied-ml for quick template).

RISKS / OPEN QUESTIONS (to resolve pre-call):
- Do they require FIPS/HSM for KMS? If yes, flag to security.
- Do they have restrictions on model checkpoints leaving their environment? Might require Private on-prem.
- Will our standard billing model map to multi-tenant feature charges? Need pricing note for per-feature cost buckets.

NEXT ACTIONS / TODO (quick):
- [ ] Verify contact emails for Ravi, Jonah, Liana (Kelsey) — target outreach Mon 3/15.
- [ ] Ask Diego to prepare a 20m tech demo deck + replay script (due 3/13).
- [ ] Draft pilot SOW template and attach trial credit clause (Anika).
- [ ] Build a short benchmark slide: p99/cost delta examples from similar customers (internal metrics).

NOTES TO SELF:
- Keep first email <6 sentences. No attachments initially except a 1-pager link.
- If they push back on budget, push the apples-to-apples replay offer: numbers beat promises.
- Use "predictable unit economics" messaging for product folks; technical folks respond to concrete p99/cost numbers and replay results.

Rough outreach schedule (two weeks):
- Week 1: tech email to Ravi + Jonah (Mon), 1 follow-up (Thu). Product email to Liana + Maya (Tue), follow-up (Fri).
- Week 2: if no reply, LinkedIn intro for Ravi + Jonah, and a short value video (30s demo clip).

Misc snippets / one-liners to A/B test:
- "Reduce fraud-scoring p99 by 2–5x without model changes"
- "Lock predictable per-feature inference bills with canary rollouts and audit logs"
- "Run an apples-to-apples replay. We'll show latency + cost delta in 7 days."

END — will flesh email variants and deck in a separate doc if we get a reply.

-- Kelsey
